During the inflationary pressures of 2022, we created our "MORTGAS" consumer misery index that is simply a sum of the price of gas ($/gallon) and the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate.

Our MORTGAS index hit a record low in the early 2020s when mortgage rates got below 3% and prices at the pump briefly got below $2/gallon.  Those days are long gone.

Gas prices first spiked in early 2022 when Russia invaded Ukraine, then they trended lower for the next few years until they spiked again this year with the US invasion of Iran.

Mortgage rates went from 3% up to 7% during the Fed's massive tightening cycle to address runaway inflation in 2022.  They too had been trending lower over the past few years, but they've moved higher again this year since the Iran War began.

Combined, our MORTGAS index is actually at a new record high right now, eclipsing the peak seen back in October 2023.  Consumers are feeling the pain as we head into midterm elections less than a month away.

zh_summary:
Over long periods of time, debts tend to rise faster than incomes, creating the long-term debt cycle.

Even as people become more indebted, lenders freely extend credit because during economic booms, incomes rise, asset values soar, and the stock market thrives. People borrow more to buy financial assets, pushing prices higher and creating a bubble.

So long as incomes keep rising, the debt burden stays manageable. But this cannot continue forever. Over decades, debt burdens slowly accumulate until debt repayments grow faster than incomes. This forces people to cut back on spending, causing incomes to fall and borrowing to dry up—eventually reversing the entire cycle.

name: Sawyer Merritt
zh_summary:
A new Tesla patent application has been published publicly today for a 3D tactile touch sensor for a humanoid robot.

These sensors could allow Optimus to detect touch, pressure, and force across different parts of its hands, improving its ability to grip and manipulate objects.

The patent says: "The separator layer can comprise a dielectric or piezoresistive material. The 3D tactile sensors can conform to curved geometries and can be used for measuring surface force, touch, and pressure. For example, the 3D tactile sensors described herein can be used in fingertips, palms, end-effectors, or other portions of a robot enabling the robot to sense the world around it. The sensors may be defined using flexible or formable material, such as thermoplastic, and can support resistive or capacitive sensing.

The 3D tactile sensors described herein can be manufactured using a variety of approaches. One example approach involves defining an array of sensing elements in a substrate material using screen printing or substrate etching. Additional approaches involve the use of 3D dispensing (e.g., 3D printing) tech-niques, pad printing techniques, or electroplating tech-niques. The substrate may be formed to a target 3D geometry using thermoforming, injection molding, or compression molding, among any other suitable techniques."

This patent was originally filed in Sept 2025. Tesla may or may not end up using this technology in Optimus: https://ppubs.uspto.gov/api/pdf/downloadPdf/US-202603

Since we first started measuring economies, GDP has only ever been able to grow three ways. Population growth, plus productivity growth, plus debt growth.

That equation is The Everything Code.

And it's what has left us in the mess we're in today. We have too few workers and too much debt. When productivity cant fill the gap, the only lever left is more debt... and the only way to carry that much debt is to debase the currency. That is why everything feels more expensive every year and why your savings never seem to keep up. 

Except now, for the first time in history, we have a way out.

AI and robots change the equation itself. They add workers that dont age, dont retire, get cheaper every year, and add productivity on a scale we've never seen. 

The catch is that it's now moving faster than society, politics or economics can adapt. Coherence breaks down. That is The Economic Singularity.

This is what my book, The Everything Code, charts. It starts with the framework itself, how debt and demographics got us here, moves through The Exponential Age and ends at The Economic Singularity. Everything Ive been working on for years, in one place and in order, so you can see why we have such a short window to position ourselves before the whole system changes completely.

It's out on November 3rd.

If you're planning to read it, I would be really grateful if you would consider pre-ordering. Pre-orders are what move the rankings, and it would mean a great deal to me.

Thanks!

BREAKING: Global central banks acquired +39 tonnes of gold in August, marking their 5th consecutive monthly purchase.

This follows +23 tonnes in July and +52 tonnes in June.

China again led demand, adding +20 tonnes and bringing its year-to-date purchases to +80 tonnes.

China’s official gold reserves have now risen to a record 2,387 tonnes, or 9% of its total FX reserves.

Furthermore, Poland bought +8 tonnes, lifting its year-to-date purchases to +98 tonnes and total gold reserves to a record 648 tonnes.

So far in 2026, central banks have acquired +170 tonnes of gold.

Central banks continue to aggressively accumulate gold.

$MRVL's investor day gave us a five-year roadmap for the photonics supply chain.

Management is targeting more than $30 in non-GAAP EPS by FY2031.

At yesterday’s Investor Day, Xi Wang described Marvell’s position in 1.6T optical connectivity:

“Today, we are at 1.6T generation, shipping in high volume, leading our competitor by two years and counting.”

That buildout also needs lasers, transceivers and silicon photonics manufacturing. The opportunity extends across $LITE $COHR $AAOI $CIEN $TSEM and $ALAB.

We followed Marvell’s roadmap through the supply chain and modeled what these businesses could be worth by 2030, accounting for their different growth markets, valuations and dilution.
